title: Build an Eval Set — Measure a Pass Rate

content.goal: A reminder as you finish and ship ATLAS.
content.why: These steps are grounded in the Phase 9 theory plus standard Groq/NIM + Python tooling. The concepts are stable; the exact API calls, library names, and model IDs are not.
content.verify: Understand this: verify the specific API calls and model names against the current provider docs (Groq, NVIDIA NIM) and library docs when you actually build — they change fast. If a call or model ID is rejected, check the provider's current docs first; that is expected, not an error in the lesson.

content.goal: Create an eval file with a handful of cases. Add evals.py.
content.why: Define success BEFORE you build. A small dataset of inputs with expected results is your regression safety net. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 15, section 15.2.)
content.code:
# evals.py
CASES = [
    {"input": "Users cannot log in at all.", "expect_severity": "BLOCKER"},
    {"input": "The footer link is the wrong shade of blue.", "expect_severity": "TRIVIAL"},
    {"input": "Checkout fails for some users intermittently.", "expect_severity": "MAJOR"},
]
content.verify: evals.py holds a few hand-picked cases with expected outcomes. Start small (10-50 is ideal); you will grow it from real failures over time.

content.goal: Write a rule-based scorer for the classifier.
content.why: When output is a fixed choice, you CAN assert precisely — this is ordinary assertion, the cheapest and most reliable scorer. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 15, section 15.4.)
content.verify: score_case returns True/False for a single case by comparing the model's severity to the expected one. Structured output (Phase 10) made this a plain assertion.

content.goal: Run each case MULTIPLE times and measure a pass rate.
content.why: Because agents are non-deterministic, "it worked once" proves nothing. A pass rate across repeated runs reveals flakiness. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 15, section 15.6.)
content.verify: Each case prints a pass rate over 5 runs. A case at 100% is robust; one at 60% is FLAKY and needs a tighter prompt, lower temperature, or better constraints. You are now quantifying reliability, not guessing.
content.troubleshoot: If everything is flaky, confirm temperature is 0 for classification and the allowed severities are named clearly in the prompt. Flakiness is a signal to tighten the spec.

content.goal: Add a threshold gate and print an overall verdict.
content.why: A threshold is your CI gate — block a change if quality drops below the bar. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 15, section 15.8.)
content.code:
def suite_passes(threshold=0.8):
    rates = [pass_rate(c) for c in CASES]
    overall = sum(rates) / len(rates)
    print(f"suite average: {overall:.0%} (threshold {threshold:.0%})")
    return overall >= threshold

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ok = suite_passes()
    print("GATE:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
content.verify: The suite prints an average and a PASS/FAIL gate. Now you can change a prompt or swap Groq to NIM, re-run, and see with EVIDENCE whether quality held.

content.goal: Grow the dataset from a real failure.
content.why: Every genuine failure becomes a new case, so it can never silently return — the flywheel that compounds quality. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 15, section 15.8.)
content.code:
# When you find ATLAS mis-classifying something, add it to CASES with the
# correct expected value, e.g.:
#   {"input": "Data is silently corrupted on save.", "expect_severity": "BLOCKER"},
# Re-run the suite; the regression is now permanently guarded.
content.verify: You added at least one case drawn from a real mistake. Re-running the suite now checks it every time.

content.goal: CHECKPOINT — you can measure whether ATLAS works.
content.why: Evaluation is the discipline that separates engineering from wishful thinking, and it lets you change things without fear.
content.verify: All true — a small eval dataset exists; a rule-based scorer grades cases; each case is run multiple times for a pass rate; a threshold gate gives a PASS/FAIL verdict; you grow the set from real failures. Next unit adds tracing so you can SEE every step in production.
